title: Directed finite-generation exhaustion of an abelian sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space whose quasi-compact open subsets form a basis. For each open $U$ put $E_U=j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_U$, with constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and open extension by zero [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero]. Every abelian sheaf $F$ on $X$ [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] admits a diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{Ab}(X)$ on a nonempty directed preordered set $I$, and compatible monomorphisms $c_i:D_i\to F$, forming a colimit cocone. Each $D_i$ admits an epimorphism $\bigoplus_{a=1}^{n_i}E_{U_{i,a}}\to D_i$ for a finite family of quasi-compact opens, allowing $n_i=0$. Both $I$ and the stalk groups may be taken in the same universe as $X$. Colimits are as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Lemma 02UX (lemma-vanishing-generated-one-section), first paragraph of the proof

proof.text: Take the disjoint union S of F(U) over all quasi-compact opens U, and let I be the finite subsets of S ordered by inclusion. The empty finite subset makes I nonempty; union gives upper bounds. This index lies in the universe of X, since both the opens and the section groups do.

For a section s on U, the constant-sheaf adjunction gives a map from the constant integer sheaf on U to F restricted to U. Extend it by zero and compose with the counit. Equivalently, on an open V contained in U, send an integer to its multiple of s restricted to V, and on other opens use the zero map; the sheafification universal property gives E_U to F. The germ of the integer 1 maps to the germ of s. For a finite subset A take the image of the coproduct of these maps. The image factorization gives a monomorphism D_A to F and an epimorphism from that finite coproduct.

Inclusion A into B gives the unique image inclusion D_A to D_B compatible with their inclusions into F; uniqueness gives identities and composition, hence a functor and a cocone. Every germ of F is represented by a section on a quasi-compact basis open inside its representing open, so is in a singleton image.

To prove the colimit universal property directly, let D_A to T be any cocone. For s in F(V), cover V by quasi-compact basis opens W and lift s restricted to W to the singleton stage (W,s restricted to W), using the distinguished integer-1 section of E_W on W. Applying the cocone gives a section of T(W). Any two local lifts become equal in the union of their finite index sets: both map to the same section of F and this union stage embeds into F. Restricting to basis opens in overlaps proves equality there, and sheaf gluing gives a unique section of T(V). Unions of finite index sets also show that this operation respects addition and restrictions. It thus defines a sheaf morphism F to T factoring all cocone maps; every section is locally such a singleton lift, so this factorization is unique. Hence F is a colimit of D. This direct universal-property proof requires neither quasi-separatedness nor a separate colimit-stalk comparison.
